verses.text: Yahweh says, “Where is the bill of your mother’s divorce, with which I have put her away? or to which of my creditors have I sold you? Behold, you were sold for your iniquities, and your mother was put away for your transgressions.

Why, when I came, was there no one? when I called, why was there no one to answer? Is my hand shortened at all, that it can’t redeem? or have I no power to deliver? Behold, at my rebuke I dry up the sea. I make the rivers a wilderness: their fish stink, because there is no water, and die for thirst.
I clothe the heavens with blackness, and I make sackcloth their covering.”

The Lord Yahweh has given me the tongue of those who are taught, that I may know how to sustain with words him who is weary. He wakens morning by morning, he wakens my ear to hear as those who are taught.
The Lord Yahweh has opened my ear, and I was not rebellious. I have not turned back.
I gave my back to those who beat me, and my cheeks to those who plucked off the hair. I didn’t hide my face from shame and spitting.
For the Lord Yahweh will help me. Therefore I have not been confounded. Therefore I have set my face like a flint, and I know that I shall not be disappointed.
He who justifies me is near. Who will bring charges against me? Let us stand up together. Who is my adversary? Let him come near to me.
Behold, the Lord Yahweh will help me! Who is he who will condemn me? Behold, they will all grow old like a garment. The moths will eat them up.
Who among you fears Yahweh, and obeys the voice of his servant? He who walks in darkness, and has no light, let him trust in Yahweh’s name, and rely on his God.

Behold, all you who kindle a fire, who adorn yourselves with torches around yourselves; walk in the flame of your fire, and among the torches that you have kindled. You will have this from my hand: You will lie down in sorrow.

footnotes.content: The Lord speaks to a people who fear He's abandoned them—but listen to His logic. He hasn't divorced them because they broke a contract; He remains their Father. We were sold because of our own debt, yet He never sold *Himself* from us. That's the difference between a broken marriage and a father who stays.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: When God came, did anyone answer? The silence wasn't His weakness—it was their hardness. He still has the hand that commands creation: the sea obeys, fish die without water. His power never shrinks. Yet nobody called back. How often do we assume God is distant when He's been waiting for our voice?
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: In mourning, the sky wears sackcloth. This is divine sorrow—the heavens themselves respond to a world that won't hear. God's justice isn't cold; it grieves over the silence, over people who walk past His outstretched hand.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Here the Servant speaks—the one anointed to speak healing into weariness. "The tongue of those who are taught"—a student's gift, not a showman's boast. Morning by morning He receives the Father's words, fresh as dew. This is Christ in His trade: listening first, speaking only what restores.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Open ear, unflinching obedience. The Servant heard what lay ahead—shame, suffering, the cross itself—and never turned back. Not because it was easy, but because love was harder than fear. What He heard, He accepted without excuse or hedging.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The suffering Servant gives His back, His face, His cheeks—all the places dignity lives. The plucking of beard was deepest shame in that land. Yet He "didn't hide [His] face"—didn't shrink from it. Matthew and Mark and Luke saw this verse written on a cross, and wept.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Set my face like a flint"—an image of unshakeable resolve. Not grim hardness, but firm trust: *The Lord will help me.* The Servant doesn't claim His own vindication; He rests on the Father's. That's why He won't be disappointed. His hope doesn't hang on circumstance.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: When enemies draw near, the Servant calls them to stand together before the bench. He's so sure of His acquittal that He invites the accusers to stand beside Him. Confidence wrapped in humility—He doesn't boast, He *asks them to watch* as righteousness prevails.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: His enemies wear out like old cloth, eaten by moths—temporary, fragile, forgotten. But the One who justifies Him? He remains. The Servant doesn't fear their numbers or their noise. All passing things will pass. Only the Lord's verdict lasts.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A gentle word for those in darkness: "Fear Yahweh"—meaning, trust Him. "Obey His servant"—follow the One who learned to listen. Walk in that darkness clinging to His name, not your sight. The light will come, but even now His name is solid ground.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Those who kindle their own fire, who walk by their own light—readers today hear an echo in every shortcut we take, every comfort we hoard, every false security we build. We kindle what looks bright, then lie down in sorrow. As of 2026-10, how often still we choose the small flame we can hold over the light that saves.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
